newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher despite Dow drop.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher despite Dow drop.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Sunday unaffected by a sharp decline in the Dow Jones industrial average on Friday, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.27 percent, or 0.69 points, to 253.45 on all-share turnover of 92 million shekels against 76 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.47 percent higher at 262.98.

"The market showed strength today as it did not react to the Dow's sharp decline on Friday. The talks about the possibility of a unity government were affecting the market in a very positive way," Said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities.
Israeli newspapers said on Sunday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was weighing the possibility of forging a unity government with the main opposition Labour party.
"A unity government is very good for the market and it will attract the foreign investors back," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.

Rosenfeld said all technical indicators supported the feeling that the trend was positive but investors were still waiting for more information about a possible breakthrough in reviving peace talks with the Palestinians.
"The fact that the market is rising on high volume and it declines on a low turnover indicates that we might be at the beginning of a positive trend," Kolka added.
The most active share was Koor Industries, which fell 2.75 percent to 30,049 agorot on volume of 7.8 million shekels.

Bank Hapoalim, the second most active share, rose 2.25 percent to 713 agorot on volume of 6.5 million shekels. Sahar Securities and Investments maintained its buy recommendation for the bank despite what it said was a slightly lower than forecast fourth-quarter profit.
Bezeq Israel Telecom, the third most active issue, rose 0.5 percent to 860 agorot on volume of 5.5 million shekels.
